blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interdisciplinary renal nutrition coordination during maintenance hemodialysis
stem: During a routine monthly review, a clinically stable client receiving maintenance hemodialysis has rising serum potassium and phosphorus trends and increasing interdialytic weight gain. Which nursing action best supports appropriate interdisciplinary management?

options.A: Review the trends with the kidney dietitian and individualize nutrition/fluid counseling to labs, intake, volume status, dialysis plan, and preferences.
options.B: Use a standard low-potassium and low-phosphorus dialysis diet first, then involve the dietitian if the laboratory abnormalities persist despite teaching.
options.C: Focus on fluid restriction for the weight gain and defer dietary potassium and phosphorus review until the dialysis prescription has been adjusted.
options.D: Ask the dietitian to eliminate potassium- and phosphorus-rich foods from the diet without considering overall intake, nutrition status, or individual preferences.

rationale: A is correct. Current CMS ESRD guidance requires an individualized comprehensive assessment by an interdisciplinary team that includes the patient, RN, ESRD physician, social worker, and dietitian. The current Appendix H requires evaluation of nutritional status by a qualified dietitian, ongoing review of laboratory values and fluid-management needs, and an individualized plan of care when nutritional problems are identified. The KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD recommends medical nutrition therapy delivered by an RDN in collaboration with the clinical team and states that MNT should be tailored to the individual's needs, nutritional status, and comorbid conditions. For CKD 3-5D, dietary phosphorus is adjusted to maintain serum phosphate in the normal range, and potassium intake should be adjusted according to serum potassium and the patient's individual needs and clinician judgment. B is incorrect because it starts with a standardized diet and delays dietitian involvement despite current abnormalities. C is incorrect because the potassium/phosphorus trends are already relevant to the nutrition assessment and should not be deferred while addressing volume status. D is incorrect because blanket elimination can undermine overall nutrition and ignores the individualized MNT framework.
educational_objective: Coordinate hemodialysis nutrition care with the kidney dietitian and individualize counseling using current laboratory, dietary, volume-status, dialysis, and patient-preference data rather than applying blanket renal-diet restrictions.
source_organization: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS); National Kidney Foundation KDOQI / Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
source_document_title: State Operations Manual Appendix H — Guidance to Surveyors: End-Stage Renal Disease Facilities; KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD: 2020 Update
source_version_date: Current CMS Appendix H revised/released in 2026 and accessed 2026-08-20; KDOQI Nutrition in CKD 2020 Update remains hosted by NKF and was rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: CMS Appendix H — §494.80 Patient assessment: PDF pages 192-199, especially V501 and V509: the IDT includes the patient/designee, RN, ESRD physician, social worker, and dietitian; assessment is individualized/comprehensive; laboratory values and fluid-management needs are assessed; nutritional status is evaluated by a qualified dietitian. §494.90(a)(2), PDF page 212: the IDT must provide care/counseling to achieve and sustain effective nutritional status; nutritional markers including sodium, calcium, phosphorus, and potassium are routinely monitored, and an individualized plan should address identified nutritional problems. KDOQI 2020 Nutrition Guideline — Statements 2.1.1-2.1.3: RDN-provided MNT in collaboration with the clinical team, tailored to individual needs/nutritional status/comorbidities with monitoring of dietary intake, body-weight changes and biochemical data. Guideline 6.3.1: adjust dietary phosphorus to maintain serum phosphate in the normal range. Guidelines 6.4.1-6.4.2: adjust dietary potassium to maintain normal serum potassium and base potassium intake on individual needs and clinician judgment when hyperkalemia/hypokalemia is present.
source_claim_supported: Current CMS ESRD requirements make nutrition assessment and care an individualized interdisciplinary process that includes a dietitian and integrates laboratory, volume and nutritional data; KDOQI supports individualized MNT and individualized potassium/phosphorus management rather than a universal fixed renal diet.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Referrals, Case Management and Continuity of Care: identify and collaborate with appropriate disciplines, coordinate individualized care, communicate significant findings, and integrate client needs/preferences and follow-up into the plan of care.
pdf_visual_verification: Direct screenshot attempts for the current CMS Appendix H nutrition-assessment and nutrition-plan pages returned CACHE MISS on 2026-08-20; no visual verification of those specific pages is claimed. Their official PDF text was retrieved. Relevant NCSBN 2026 Management of Care collaboration/referral content had been visually verified earlier in this audit session. KDOQI content was verified from the guideline's indexed full-text/official NKF overview; no unverified screenshot claim is made.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'hemodialysis dietitian potassium phosphorus individualized nutrition fluid interdialytic weight gain' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the renal-nutrition coordination construct but removed the universal-diet and 'all potassium/phosphorus' cueing. The revised item tests realistic management errors: starting a standardized diet before individualized dietitian review, treating volume management as a reason to defer concurrent electrolyte-nutrition assessment, and using blanket food elimination that ignores overall nutrition and patient-specific needs. Adversarial reread added routine-review/clinical-stability context so rising potassium cannot be misread as an unspecified acute emergency requiring a different first action.

option_audit.A: Correct; integrates CMS-required IDT/dietitian assessment with KDOQI individualized MNT and current potassium/phosphorus/volume data.
option_audit.B: Plausible protocol-first error; incorrect because the client's abnormal trends warrant individualized dietitian assessment rather than a standard diet followed by delayed referral.
option_audit.C: Plausible single-problem sequencing error; incorrect because volume status and potassium/phosphorus nutrition issues should be evaluated concurrently rather than deferring the latter.
option_audit.D: Plausible overrestriction error; incorrect because potassium/phosphorus management is individualized and must preserve overall nutritional adequacy.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Options contain comparable interdisciplinary-management detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel management actions in the same hemodialysis nutrition scenario.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after acute-context clarification, CMS/KDOQI source-based audit, and targeted repository search.
